habitat: Pairs and small parties around human habitation, including towns, small settlements and isolated permanent camps. It breeds under the eaves of houses.
summary: A very common resident, and an introduced species. The male has a grey crown, a dark brown nape grading into a chestnut back and wings, a small white wing-bar, and black from the lores to a variable bib. The female and immature are paler, with a pink bill and pink legs. The call is chissip or chee-ip. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: The female Cape Sparrow is richer in colour, with a greyer head and a black bill. The female House Sparrow is paler, with a pink bill.

research.note: Newman calls it a very common resident and an introduced species, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The female and immature are only described as paler, with a pink bill and pink legs, which is why this needs review. Great Sparrow is the comparison Newman names and is not in this list. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
